sanskrit: brahmagavī pacyamānā yāvat sābhi vijaṅgahe | tejo rāṣṭrasya nir hanti na vīro jāyate pumān ||
english: As long as the brahmin's cow, being cooked, is tossed about, it destroys the brilliance of the kingdom; no hero, no man, is born there.

sanskrit: ākramaṇena vai devā dviṣanto ghnanti pūruṣam | steyādaṃ brahmajyaṃ kṣetre cānṛtavādinam ||
english: Verily it is by treading down that the gods smite the man they hate — the thief, the one who wrongs a brahmin, the one who speaks falsehood in a legal dispute.

sanskrit: viṣam etad devakṛtaṃ rājā varuṇo abravīt | na brāhmaṇasya gāṃ jagdhvā rāṣṭre jāgāra kaś cana ||
english: "This is a poison fashioned by the gods," so spoke King Varuṇa: "After eating the brahmin's cow, no one in the kingdom prospers."

sanskrit: tad vai rāṣṭram ā sravati bhinnāṃ nāvam ivodakam | brāhmaṇo yatra jīyate tad rāṣṭraṃ hanti ducchunā ||
english: That kingdom drains away like water through a broken boat; in the land where a brahmin is oppressed, ill-fortune destroys the kingdom.

sanskrit: ekaśataṃ vai janatā bhūmir yā vyadhūnuta | prajāṃ hiṃsitvā brāhmaṇīm asaṃbhavyaṃ parābhavan ||
english: A hundred and one peoples did the earth shake off; having injured the brahmin's progeny, they fell to irreversible ruin.

sanskrit: yām udājann ṛṣayo manīṣiṇaḥ śramasātāṃ bṛhatīṃ devajūtām | sā brahmajyaṃ pacati pacyamānā rāṣṭram asya bṛhatī yac ca varcaḥ ||
english: She whom the wise seers drove forth — the great one, hard-won by toil, impelled by the gods — she, being cooked, cooks away the brahmin-offense along with the kingdom of him who holds her, and his splendour.

sanskrit: vācā brāhmaṇam ṛcchati jāmi hanty acittyā | mitrāya satye druhyati yaṃ devā ghnanti pūruṣam ||
english: He who assails a brahmin with words, who through ignorance slays a kinsman, who betrays a friend through falsehood — that man the gods smite.

sanskrit: ekapāc chanda ekakāmaṃ ca | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe prathamayā rātryā prathamayā samidhā ||
english: The single-footed metre and the single desire — he attains that and holds it fast, with the first night-watch and the first fuel-stick.

sanskrit: dvipāc chando dvipadaś ca paśūn | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe dvitīyayā rātryā dvitīyayā samidhā ||
english: The two-footed metre and the two-footed cattle — he attains those and holds them fast, with the second night-watch and the second fuel-stick.

sanskrit: trīṃl lokāṃs trīṃl lokapatīn | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe tṛtiyayā rātryā tṛtīyayā samidhā ||
english: The three worlds and the three lords of worlds — he attains those and holds them fast, with the third night-watch and the third fuel-stick.

sanskrit: catuṣpāc chandaś catuṣpadaś ca paśūn | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe caturthyā rātryā caturthyā samidhā ||
english: The four-footed metre and the four-footed cattle — he attains those and holds them fast, with the fourth night-watch and the fourth fuel-stick.

sanskrit: pañca diśaḥ pañca pradiśaḥ | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe pañcamyā rātryā pañcamyā samidhā ||
english: The five cardinal directions and the five intermediate directions — he attains those and holds them fast, with the fifth night-watch and the fifth fuel-stick.

sanskrit: traiṣṭubhaṃ chando virājaṃ svarājaṃ samrājam | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe saṣṭhyā rātryā ṣaṣṭhyā samidhā ||
english: The Triṣṭubh metre, the Virāj, the Svarāj, and the Samrāj — he attains those and holds them fast, with the sixth night-watch and the sixth fuel-stick.

sanskrit: sapta prāṇān saptāpānān sapta ṛṣīṃś ca | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe saptamyā rātryā saptamyā samidhā ||
english: The seven vital breaths, the seven downward breaths, and the seven seers — he attains those and holds them fast, with the seventh night-watch and the seventh fuel-stick.

sanskrit: ojaś ca tejaś ca sahaś ca balaṃ ca | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe aṣṭamyā rātryā aṣṭamyā samidhā ||
english: Vital potency, brilliance, might, and strength — he attains those and holds them fast, with the eighth night-watch and the eighth fuel-stick.

sanskrit: ambhaś ca mahaś cānnaṃ cānnādyaṃ ca | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe navamyā rātryā navamyā samidhā ||
english: The waters, the Great One, food, and the eating of food — he attains those and holds them fast, with the ninth night-watch and the ninth fuel-stick.

sanskrit: brahma ca kṣatraṃ cendriyaṃ ca brāhmaṇavarcasaṃ ca | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe daśamyā rātryā daśamyā samidhā ||
english: The brahman power, the kṣatra power, sovereign capacity, and the radiance of brahmin excellence — he attains those and holds them fast, with the tenth night-watch and the tenth fuel-stick.

sanskrit: viśvāvasū ca sarvavasū ca | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe ekādaśyā rātryā ekādaśyā samidhā ||
english: Viśvāvasu and all the Vasus — he attains those and holds them fast, with the eleventh night-watch and the eleventh fuel-stick.

sanskrit: pāṅktaṃ chandaḥ prajāpatiṃ saṃvatsaram | tad āpnoti cāva ca rundhe dvādaśyā rātryā dvādaśyā samidhā ||
english: The Pāṅkta metre, Prajāpati, and the Year — he attains those and holds them fast, with the twelfth night-watch and the twelfth fuel-stick.

sanskrit: yo vā ekaśarāvaṃ nirvaped ekarṣim evānu nir vapet | eṣa vā ekarṣir yad agniḥ | ekarṣiṃ caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe ekarṣir iva tapaty ekarṣir iva dīdāyaikarṣir ivānnādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda | sa ya evaṃ vidvān prāśnīyād etām eva devatāṃ manasā dhyāyed ekarṣes tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmy ekarṣes tvā hastābhyām ā rabha ekarṣes tvāsyena prāśnāmy ekarṣes tvā jaṭhare sādayāmīti | sa yathā hutam iṣṭaṃ prāśnīyād evainaṃ prāśnāti ||
english: He who would offer a single bowl-portion — he offers it as it were to the One Seer. For that One Seer is Agni. He wins both the One Seer and a world. He blazes like the One Seer, he shines like the One Seer, he becomes an eater of food like the One Seer — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon this very deity with his mind: "With the eye of the One Seer I behold thee; with the two hands of the One Seer I take hold of thee; with the mouth of the One Seer I eat thee; in the belly of the One Seer I establish thee." He eats of it just as one eats of what has been duly offered in sacrifice.

sanskrit: yo vai dviśarāvaṃ nirvapet prāṇāpānāv evānu nir vapet | etau vai prāṇāpānau yan mātariśvā cāgniś ca | prāṇāpānau caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe jyog jīvati sarvam āyur eti na purā jarasaḥ pramīyate yaḥ (…) | sa ya evaṃ vidvān) praśnīyād etām eva devate manasā dhyāyet prāṇāpānayos tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi prāṇāpānayos tvā hastābhyām ā rabhe prāṇāpānayos tvāsyena prāśnāmi prāṇāpānayos tvā jaṭhare (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a two-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to Prāṇa and Apāna. For those two, Prāṇa and Apāna, are Mātariśvan and Agni. He wins both Prāṇa and Apāna and a world; he lives long, reaches his full span of life, and does not die before old age — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon these two deities with his mind: "With the eye of Prāṇa-and-Apāna I behold thee; with the two hands of Prāṇa-and-Apāna I take hold of thee; with the mouth of Prāṇa-and-Apāna I eat thee; in the belly of Prāṇa-and-Apāna I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai triśarāvaṃ nirvapet trīṇy eva trikadrukāṇy anu nir vapet | etāni vai trīṇi trikadrukāṇi yad ṛcaḥ sāmāni yajūṃṣi brāhmaṇam | brahma caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe brāhmaṇavarcasī bhavati yaḥ (…) (…) prāśnīyād etām eva devatāṃ manasā dhyāyed brahmaṇas tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi brahmaṇas tvā hastābhyām ā rabhe brahmaṇas tvāsyena prāśnāmi brahmaṇas tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a three-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to the three trikadruka vessels. For those three trikadruka vessels are the Ṛk verses, the Sāmans, the Yajus formulas, and the Brāhmaṇa. He wins both brahman power and a world; he becomes endowed with the brilliance of brahminhood — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon this deity with his mind: "With the eye of Brahman I behold thee; with the two hands of Brahman I take hold of thee; with the mouth of Brahman I eat thee; in the belly of Brahman I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai catuḥśarāvaṃ nirvapec catasra evorvīr anu nir vapet | etā vai catasra urvīr yad diśaḥ | diśaś caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe kalpante asmai diśo diśāṃ priyo bhavati yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśnīyād etām eva devatāṃ manasā dhyāyed diśāṃ tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi diśāṃ tvā hastābhyām ā rabhe diśāṃ tvāsyena prāśnāmi diśāṃ tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a four-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to the four broad expanses. For those four broad expanses are the directions. He wins both the directions and a world; the directions serve him well, and he becomes dear to the directions — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon this deity with his mind: "With the eye of the Directions I behold thee; with the two hands of the Directions I take hold of thee; with the mouth of the Directions I eat thee; in the belly of the Directions I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai pañcaśarāvaṃ nirvaped vaiśvānaram eva pañcamūrdhānam anu nir vapet | eṣa vai vaiśvānaraḥ pañcamūrdhā yad dyauś ca pṛthivī ca mātariśvā cāgniś cājasrā cātapan | vaiśvānaraṃ caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe vaiśvānara iva tapati vaiśvānara iva dīdāya vaiśvānara ivānnādo bhavati yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśniyād etām eva devatāṃ manasā dhyāyed vaiśvānarasya tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi vaiśvānarasya tvā hastābhyām ā rabhe vaiśvānarasya tvāsyena prāśnāmi vaiśvānarasya tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a five-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to Vaiśvānara of five heads. For that Vaiśvānara of five heads is Heaven, Earth, Mātariśvan, Agni, and the ever-shining Sun. He wins both Vaiśvānara and a world; he blazes like Vaiśvānara, he shines like Vaiśvānara, he becomes an eater of food like Vaiśvānara — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon this deity with his mind: "With the eye of Vaiśvānara I behold thee; with the two hands of Vaiśvānara I take hold of thee; with the mouth of Vaiśvānara I eat thee; in the belly of Vaiśvānara I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai ṣaṭśarāvaṃ nirvapet ṣaḍ yāvna eva devān anu nir vapet | ete vai ṣaḍ yāvāno devā yad ṛtavaḥ | ṛtūṃś caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe kalpante asmā ṛtavo na ṛtuṣv āvṛścata ṛtūnāṃ priyo bhavati yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśnīyād etā eva devatā manasā dhyāyed ṛtūnāṃ tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmy ṛtūnāṃ tvā hastābhyām ā rabha ṛtūnāṃ tvāsyena prāśnāmy ṛtūnāṃ tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a six-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to the six way-going gods. For those six way-going gods are the seasons. He wins both the seasons and a world; the seasons serve him well, he is not cut off in the seasons, and he becomes dear to the seasons — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon these very deities with his mind: "With the eye of the Seasons I behold thee; with the two hands of the Seasons I take hold of thee; with the mouth of the Seasons I eat thee; in the belly of the Seasons I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai saptaśarāvaṃ nirvapet sapta ṛṣīn evānu nir vapet | ete vai sapta ṛṣayo yat prāṇāpānavyānāḥ | saptarṣīṃś caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe jyog jīvati sarvam āyur eti na purā jarasaḥ pramīyate yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśnīyād etā eva devatā manasā dhyāyet saptarṣīṇāṃ tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi saptarṣīṇāṃ tvā hastābhyām ā rabhe saptarṣīṇāṃ tvāsyena prāśnāmi saptarṣīṇāṃ tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a seven-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to the Seven Seers. For those Seven Seers are the prāṇa, apāna, and vyāna breaths. He wins both the Seven Seers and a world; he lives long, reaches his full span of life, and does not die before old age — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon these very deities with his mind: "With the eye of the Seven Seers I behold thee; with the two hands of the Seven Seers I take hold of thee; with the mouth of the Seven Seers I eat thee; in the belly of the Seven Seers I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vā aṣṭaśarāvaṃ nirvaped virājam evavāṣṭāpadīm anu nir vapet | eṣā vai virāḍ aṣṭāpadī yad dyauś ca pṛthivī cāpaś cauṣadhayaś ca vāyuś cāntarikṣaṃ ca sūryaś ca candramāś ca | virājaṃ caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe vi rājaty asmiṃś ca loke amuṣmiṃś ca vairāja rṣabha ity enam āhur yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśnīyād etām eva devatāṃ manasā dhyāyed virājas tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi virājas tvā hastābhyām ā rabhe virājas tvāsyena prāśnāmi virājas tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer an eight-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to the Virāj, the eight-footed one. For that Virāj, the eight-footed one, is Heaven, Earth, the Waters, the Plants, Wind, Atmosphere, Sun, and Moon. He wins both the Virāj and a world; he shines forth in this world and in yonder world; they call him "a bull of the Virāj" — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon this very deity with his mind: "With the eye of the Virāj I behold thee; with the two hands of the Virāj I take hold of thee; with the mouth of the Virāj I eat thee; in the belly of the Virāj I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai navaśarāvaṃ nirvapen nava yāvna eva devān anu nirvapet | ete vai navayāvāno devā yan māsāḥ | māsaś caiva lokaṃ cava rundhe kalpante asmai māsā māsāṃ priyo bhavati yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśnīyād etā eva devatā manasā dhyāyen māsāṃ tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi māsāṃ tvā hastābhyām ā rabhe māsāṃ tvāsyena prāśnāmi māsāṃ tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a nine-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to the nine way-going gods. For those nine way-going gods are the months. He wins both the months and a world; the months serve him well, and he becomes dear to the months — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon these very deities with his mind: "With the eye of the Months I behold thee; with the two hands of the Months I take hold of thee; with the mouth of the Months I eat thee; in the belly of the Months I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai daśaśarāvaṃ nirvaped iḍām eva dhenum anu nirvapet | esā vā iḍā dhenur yad yajñaḥ paśavaḥ | iḍāṃ caiva dhenuṃ yajñaṃ ca lokaṃ ca paśūṃś cāva rundhe kalpante asmā iḍa iḍāṃ priyo bhavati yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśnīyad etām eva devatāṃ manasā dhyāyed iḍāyās tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi- -iḍāyās tvā hastābhyām ā rabha iḍāyās tvāsyena prāśnāmi- -iḍāyās tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer a ten-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to Iḍā the milk-cow. For that Iḍā the milk-cow is sacrifice and cattle. He wins both Iḍā the milk-cow and sacrifice and a world and cattle; the Iḍā offerings serve him well, and he becomes dear to Iḍā — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon this very deity with his mind: "With the eye of Iḍā I behold thee; with the two hands of Iḍā I take hold of thee; with the mouth of Iḍā I eat thee; in the belly of Iḍā I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vā ekādaśaśarāvaṃ nirvaped rohitam evānu nir vapet | eṣa vai rohito yad indraḥ | indraṃ caiva lokaṃ cāva rundhe indriyāvī priya indrasya bhavati yaḥ (…) | (…) prāśnīyād etām eva devatāṃ manasā dhyāyed indrasya tvā cakṣuṣā paśyāmi- -indrasya tvā hastābhyām ā rabha indrasya tvāsyena prāśnāmi- -indrasya tvā (…) | (…) ||
english: He who would offer an eleven-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to Rohita. For that Rohita is Indra. He wins both Indra and a world; he becomes possessed of sovereign power and dear to Indra — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon this very deity with his mind: "With the eye of Indra I behold thee; with the two hands of Indra I take hold of thee; with the mouth of Indra I eat thee; in the belly of Indra I place thee."

sanskrit: yo vai dvādaśaśarāvaṃ nirvaped viśvām eva devān anu nir vapet | ete vai viśve devā yad idaṃ sarvam | viśvāṃś caiva devām̐l lokaṃ cāva rundhe kalpante asmai viśve devāḥ priyo viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda | sa ya evaṃ vidvān prāśnīyād etā eva devatā manasā dhyāyed viśveṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ cakṣuṣā paśyāmi viśveṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ hastābhyām ā rabhe viśveṣāṃ tvā devānām āsyena prāśnāmi viśveṣāṃ tvā devānāṃ jaṭhare sādayāmīti | sa yathā hutam iṣṭaṃ prāśnīyād evainaṃ prāśnāti ||
english: He who would offer a twelve-bowl portion — he offers it as it were to all the Viśve Devāḥ. For those Viśve Devāḥ are all this universe. He wins both the Viśve Devāḥ and a world; all the Viśve Devāḥ serve him well, and he becomes dear to all the gods — he who knows thus. He who, knowing thus, would eat of it, should meditate upon these very deities with his mind: "With the eye of all the gods I behold thee; with the two hands of all the gods I take hold of thee; with the mouth of all the gods I eat thee; in the belly of all the gods I establish thee." He eats of it just as one eats of what has been duly offered in sacrifice.
